private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate earned approximately $74,700 on 498 allocated hours. Birchwood charged $325 and Calder charged $350. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how strongly allocations respond to price.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $325 rate undercut both competitors’ $350 rates and yielded 821 allocated hours and about $102,619 in profit. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how strongly hours respond to price.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly while remaining below both competitors. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 to assess whether the higher margin offsets any lost volume; continue adjusting for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 498 hours and earned about $74,690. Competitors charged $350 and $325. We have only one quarter of allocation data, so price sensitivity remains uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest rate increase while monitoring allocated hours and the next panel rate card. Avoid large changes until we can estimate how volume responds to price.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $340 for Q3 to preserve the improved volume and margin without initiating a further price cut. Reassess after seeing Q3 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $325 in Q1 to $340 in Q2 coincided with hours falling from 821 to 688 and reported quarterly profit falling from $102,619 to $96,295. Competitor rates also changed, so the effect of our rate alone is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Return to $325 to seek more hours while maintaining a $125 margin per hour. Compare Q3 hours and profit with prior quarters before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $350 to $365 coincided with hours falling from 498 to 417 and quarterly profit declining from about $74,690 to $68,836. Competitors’ average rate stayed near $340, so our premium widened.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate modestly to regain hours while preserving a meaningful margin. Use Q3 allocation to assess whether the Q2 decline was primarily price-driven.

private_notes.observations: At $340, allocated hours fell from 688 in Q2 to 562 in Q3 as both other firms lowered their rates. Q3 profit was approximately $78,743, down from $96,295 in Q2.
